tagline: One local control plane for the AI engines you choose.

features.name: Guided llama.cpp setup
features.description: Configure an existing local llama-server executable, GGUF model, CPU/GPU layer mode (including llama.cpp automatic layer placement), context size and localhost port from the dashboard; paths are saved on the device.

features.name: Engine readiness checks
features.description: The dashboard distinguishes a running process from a model server that answers its local health endpoint, and chat stays disabled until the default engine is ready.

features.name: Local-first runtime
features.description: The control API binds to loopback by default. Model inference stays in the engine you configure.

features.name: Local device inventory
features.description: The dashboard reports local OS/architecture, logical CPU count, total/available system RAM, free user-data disk space and graphics adapters when the platform probe supports them (Windows DXGI and Linux DRM/sysfs). This information stays on the computer. Detecting a GPU or installing a CUDA package is not proof that inference used the GPU.

features.name: Managed engine and model downloads
features.description: The reviewed starter catalog contains the official llama.cpp CPU package, CUDA 12/13 server packages with their matching official CUDA runtime/DLL dependencies, and a pinned Qwen2.5 1.5B GGUF starter model. Each asset is SHA-256 verified and safely extracted before activation; real GPU task validation remains a separate evidence gate.

features.name: Local diagnostic reports
features.description: Keeps runtime/download lifecycle events locally and lets the user export a sanitized report with current jobs and engine readiness. Engine process logs are opt-in; no diagnostics are uploaded automatically.

features.name: Engine lifecycle
features.description: Start and stop explicitly configured engine processes, inspect process state, and keep per-engine logs. A real inference engine and model must be installed separately in this alpha.

features.name: OpenAI-style chat proxy
features.description: Forward non-streaming chat requests to a local OpenAI-compatible engine.

features.name: Cross-platform CI
features.description: One canonical workflow validates pull requests and builds/tests Windows x64, Linux x64, macOS Intel x64 and macOS Apple Silicon arm64. Main pushes publish preview artifacts and deploy the website only after all four target jobs pass their extracted-package health checks.

features.name: macOS runtime packages
features.description: The canonical pipeline builds and smoke-tests separate macOS Intel and Apple Silicon command-line packages. Homebrew dylib dependencies are bundled, while macOS system libraries remain required; preview packages are not Developer ID signed or notarized.

features.name: Release downloads and checksums
features.description: Versioned releases publish a Windows x64 desktop setup installer and portable ZIP, Linux x64, macOS Intel x64 and macOS Apple Silicon arm64 packages, plus a SHA-256 manifest after every platform build/package gate passes.

features.name: Automatic preview packages
features.description: Every main push uses one pipeline run: Windows, Linux, macOS x64 and macOS arm64 build/test/package jobs run in parallel; the GitHub Pages deployment runs last and only when all four pass. Preview archives are retained for 14 days; version tags publish Releases after all package checks.

features.name: Windows desktop installer
features.description: Per-user Windows setup (.exe), dedicated WebView2 desktop window, Start menu and optional desktop shortcuts, tray controls, console-free runtime startup, and uninstall that preserves user data. New desktop builds include a user-confirmed in-app update using the official full setup package, GitHub SHA-256/size verification, full-install backup, health verification, rollback and interruption recovery. The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows may show an unknown-publisher/SmartScreen warning.

features.name: Hardware-aware model setup
features.description: A first local device inventory is available in the dashboard. CPU feature and driver discovery, reliable VRAM/runtime evidence, measured compatibility profiles, and evidence-backed engine/backend/model recommendations with safe fallbacks remain planned.

features.name: Portable package launch (alpha)
features.description: Portable archives remain available as a fallback and for Linux/macOS preview builds. Windows also has a per-user desktop setup installer in the v0.1.2-alpha release. Portable launchers are compatibility paths, not the preferred Windows user experience.

features.name: Audio, vision and embeddings
features.description: Add isolated adapters after the first engine lifecycle and security contracts are stable.

features.name: MCP integration
features.description: Expose selected runtime operations through a deliberately limited, localhost-only MCP adapter.

features.name: Verified runtime updates
features.description: The dashboard checks official GitHub Releases and verifies matching packages before staging. Tagged portable Windows ZIP installs support confirmed apply/restart and rollback. Installed Windows desktop builds that include the desktop updater can apply the full official setup installer with a verified full-install backup, health check, rollback and interrupted-update recovery. Linux/macOS currently stage only and require manual application archive replacement.

features.name: Installed Windows desktop updates
features.description: New installed desktop builds can download the exact official setup asset, verify its SHA-256 and size, shut down the local runtime gracefully, back up the full app directory, update shell and runtime together, confirm local health and restore the previous installation after failure or interruption. User settings, engines, models and logs remain outside the application directory. Publisher signing and clean Windows 10/11 manual acceptance remain outstanding.

securityNotes: Only localhost/loopback is supported by default.

The built-in component downloader accepts only reviewed catalog IDs, uses HTTPS-only transfer, validates expected size and SHA-256, checks the GGUF header, and rejects archive traversal/link/special-file entries. It does not accept arbitrary URLs.

Engine release SHA-256 metadata is fetched from the official upstream GitHub API; this verifies integrity against that metadata but is not a cryptographic signature or independent publisher attestation.

No usage telemetry or silent executable replacement is enabled. Update checks request public release metadata from GitHub. Windows portable-release updates require user confirmation and a verified local rollback copy; Linux/macOS currently require manual application archive replacement after verification. SHA-256 checks do not replace publisher signatures or provenance attestation.
The API has no authentication. Do not expose the runtime or setup API to a LAN or public internet.

The Windows alpha installer is not code-signed and may trigger an unknown-publisher/SmartScreen warning. Do not bypass Windows protection to disguise this; release signing requires a real publisher certificate, secure CI key custody and timestamping.
